text:
ana: kicked off a synthetic longwrap KV bench to stress fragmentation/reuse across long contexts. comparing baseline -> patch-A results. quick summary: baseline shows steady mem drift, patch-A looks much better. attaching numbers below.

omar: can you drop the exact command and config so i can repro locally? also which model/seq len?

ana: (typo) ana: run command: `./bench_longwrap --model gpt-7b --seq 32768 --tokens 500000 --kv-reuse-threshold 0.7`
config for A: `--kv-reuse-threshold 0.85 --kv-compact-interval 10000 --batch-window-ms 10`

rachel: were kernels pinned? kernel selector sometimes picks the fallback matmul for long sequences and that can increase memory working set (we saw this on the A100 perf matrix).

ana: ana: yep pinned to `fast-attn-fused` via KERNEL_HINT=fast-attn-fused for both runs to keep that constant. also forced continuous batching off for the baseline run, then tried continuous batching=on in a follow-up to see batching impact.

ben: pprof snapshot shows hot paths: `kv_cache_compact()` and `slab_allocator::alloc_slowpath`. flamegraph: https://internal.dev/pprof/2201234567/flame (link internal)

ana: ana: numbers (summary):
- baseline: RSS start 2.12GB -> end 2.37GB (+250MB) after 500k tokens; fragmentation metric (free_extents_ratio) 0.27 -> 0.48; reuse_hits 0.62
- patch-A (reuse threshold 0.85 + compact interval 10k): RSS start 2.10GB -> end 2.15GB (+40MB); fragmentation 0.28 -> 0.31; reuse_hits 0.79
- batching experiment (continuous batching window 64): peak RSS up by ~30MB, tail latency 12% better, throughput unchanged

ana: ana: heap histogram sample (top entries):
```
# bytes  count  object
120MB   512    kv_extent
90MB    8      slab_arena
45MB    2048   small_kv_frag
```

omar: nice. did you simulate interleaved contexts (short+long) or just pure long streams? fragmentation often spikes when mixing lengths.

ana: ana: we did 3 mixes: pure-long, 80/20 short-long interleave, and randomized interleave. fragmentation worst with random interleave on baseline (free_extents_ratio up to 0.52). patch-A keeps it under 0.34 across mixes.

rachel: sounds like reuse threshold + compaction interval is doing the heavy lifting. but we should check kernel selection heuristics: if selector changes for larger batches it might alter L1/L2 pressure and indirectly affect slab fragmentation. can we add a kernel trace to the regtest?

ben: agree. also add a p99 alloc latency metric to the suite so we can detect regressions where compaction adds latency spikes.

ana: ana: will add both. plan: create deterministic regtest that replays RNG seeds + interleave pattern; run 1M token warmup then track RSS, fragmentation, reuse_hits, p99-alloc, and kernel selection timeline.

omar: do we want CI to gate on delta > 100MB RSS or fragmentation raising >0.1?

rachel: suggest gating: RSS regression > 150MB OR fragmentation delta > 0.15 OR reuse_hits drop > 0.1. keep thresholds conservative to avoid noise.

ci-bot: nightly-kvcache-longwrap: passed ✅ (2201234600)

ana: ana: i'll open a PR with the regtest and a shortwriteup of the bench harness + how to run locally. cc @omar @ben for review. thanks! :party:
